doc.When to use:
Answers from an assistant that searched your docs, the web or connected tools and should show where each claim comes from
Research, support or knowledge-base products where people need to check the source before they act
doc.When not to use:
Casual chat without sources – a plain message bubble is lighter
Long documents or code – the answer is made for a few paragraphs and lists
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Tab	Moves through source cards, citation chips, follow-ups and actions
Esc	Closes the source preview of the focused chip
doc.Accessibility:
Citation chips are buttons named after their sources; the preview is a tooltip linked to the chip
The answer is marked busy while it streams, so screen readers read it once it's complete
Copy, feedback and status changes are announced in a polite live region
doc.Motion:
Source cards pop in one after another while the label reads "Reading 6 sources"
Words fade in out of a light blur, citation chips pop in, a pulsing dot marks where the text grows
Hovering a chip lights up its source card, hovering a card lights up its chips
The card glides to its new height; with prefers-reduced-motion the answer appears at once
doc.Responsive behavior:
Fills its container up to 640px; source cards scroll sideways on narrow screens
Tap a citation chip to open its preview on touch screens
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Streamed answer with source cards, citation chips that preview their source, copy, regenerate, feedback and follow-ups.

doc.When to use:
The main input of an AI assistant or agent that can act on connected tools
Flows where the user has to grant extra permissions before a run
doc.When not to use:
Plain chat between people – a simple text field with a send button is enough
Very narrow spaces below ~280px, where the toolbar labels get too small
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Enter	Send the message
Shift + Enter	New line
↑ or ↓	Open the model picker and move through it
Home or End	Jump to the first or last model
Enter or Space	Pick the highlighted model (in the picker)
Esc	Close the model picker or discard a recording
doc.Accessibility:
Loading and result states are announced through a polite live region
Busy buttons expose aria-busy; the hidden tray row is inert and aria-hidden
Clicking anywhere on the white card focuses the message field
The model picker is a listbox with aria-activedescendant, so screen readers follow the highlight
doc.Motion:
Connecting apps runs two shimmer sweeps while the logos hop, then the card slides down to reveal “Select a project”
Requesting approval waves the hand, then morphs into the “Unrestricted access” pill
The model picker morphs out of the corner next to its button, opens toward the side with more room and stays inside the visible frame
A hover fill fades in under the pointer and glides between rows
While recording, the heard words appear in gray and turn dark once confirmed; a dotted audio trace scrolls next to the controls
All transitions collapse to instant changes with prefers-reduced-motion
doc.Responsive behavior:
Fills its container up to 680px wide; all sizes follow the width via container query units and stop growing at a compact maximum
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Prompt composer with model picker, voice input, app connections and approval request.

doc.When to use:
Showing what an AI assistant is doing while it works: searching, reading, drafting
Long-running tasks where a visible trail of steps builds trust and keeps people waiting patiently
doc.When not to use:
Short waits under a second – a simple spinner or shimmer is enough
Exact progress you can measure – use a progress bar with a percentage
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Enter or Space	Collapse or expand the steps (on the header), or show more sources
Tab	Move through the source links – each shows its tooltip on focus
doc.Accessibility:
The header is a button with aria-expanded, so the steps can be collapsed
New steps are announced politely through an aria-live list
doc.Motion:
The header shimmers with a live timer while thinking, then turns into “Worked for …”
Steps fade up one after another and the timeline grows down to each new node
Sources pop in one by one; the active step pulses and shimmers
Hovering a source shows its link as a tooltip; “+N more” reveals the remaining sources
At the end a blue check pops in and draws its tick
With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears without animation
doc.Responsive behavior: Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: AI working panel with a live timer, searched sources and thinking steps that appear one by one.

doc.When to use:
A small AI helper inside an editor, CRM or sidebar – rewrite, shorten, translate or draft
Landing pages that should show an assistant you can actually try, including voice input
doc.When not to use:
Long conversations with files, tools and model settings – use the Chat Composer or the AI Workspace block
When you can't send voice to the browser's speech service – set speech="simulate" or hide the mic
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Enter	Sends what's in the prompt field
Shift or Enter	Starts a new line – the field grows up to four lines, then scrolls
Tab	Moves through the suggestions, the field, Send, the mic and New chat
doc.Accessibility:
The mic is a toggle button with aria-pressed and a label that says what it does next
New messages are announced politely; the typing dots carry a label
Everything works with the keyboard; dictation is optional
doc.Motion:
The glow keeps drifting in the lower half; the welcome view hands over to the chat with a short rise
While listening, the mic turns dark with three calm bars and a soft ring breathing outwards; words appear live in the field
When you stop speaking, the finished sentence moves into the chat as your message; replies stream in word by word
With prefers-reduced-motion the glow stands still and replies appear at once
doc.Responsive behavior:
Fills its container up to 380px wide
Dictation uses the Web Speech API (Chrome, Edge, Safari) with the page language; elsewhere a short simulated take plays
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: AI chat card with a soft gradient glow, suggestions, streaming replies and live voice dictation.

doc.When to use:
Two-step sign-in, email or phone verification, confirming a sensitive action with a one-time code
Any short code people copy from an email or SMS – paste and autofill fill every box at once
doc.When not to use:
Codes longer than about 8 characters or with free-form text – a plain text field is easier to read and correct
Passwords or PINs that must stay hidden – the boxes show what's typed
doc.Keyboard interactions:
0–9	Fills the active box and moves on; typing on a filled box replaces it
⌫	Clears the box and goes back one
← or →	Moves between the filled boxes and the next empty one
Home or End	Jumps to the first box, or to the next empty one
⌘ or V	Pastes a whole code – spaces and dashes are ignored
doc.Accessibility:
One real text input carries the whole code, so screen readers hear one field ("Verification code, 6 digits") instead of six
autocomplete="one-time-code" lets iOS and Android offer the code from an SMS; inputMode="numeric" opens the number pad
Errors set aria-invalid and point to the message with aria-describedby; verifying, errors, success and resend are announced in a polite live region
doc.Motion:
A single focus ring glides from box to box with a softly blinking caret; digits pop in out of a short blur
Pasted or autofilled codes fill the boxes one after another
Verifying: a soft light passes over the boxes. Error: a calm shake, red borders, the message grows in below and the code fades out for the next try
Success: the boxes slide together while one frame morphs its width into a "Verified" pill and the check draws in
With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly
doc.Responsive behavior:
Container query: the boxes shrink to fit their container – six boxes with a separator fit a 320px phone
Inputs use 16px text under the hood, so iOS doesn't zoom in on focus
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: The verification code field done right – a gliding focus ring, paste and SMS autofill, a calm shake on errors and a morph into Verified.

doc.When to use:
Onboarding, checkout or setup wizards where one long form would feel like too much at once
Flows whose later steps depend on earlier answers, ending in a review before anything is created
doc.When not to use:
Two or three fields – a single form is faster
Settings people jump around in freely – use tabs or sections instead
doc.Keyboard interactions:
↵	Continues (in a chip field: adds the typed entry first, Continue when it's empty)
Tab	Moves through the fields, then Back and Continue
← or →	In the plan cards: moves and selects; ↵ picks and continues
, or ⌫	In a chip field: comma adds, Backspace in the empty field removes the last chip
doc.Accessibility:
The steps are an ordered list with aria-current="step"; finished steps are buttons that jump back
On narrow screens the list stays for screen readers while the compact "Step 2 of 4" text shows on screen
The new step's first field (or its heading) gets the focus; after a failed Continue the first invalid field does
Fields carry aria-invalid and point to their message with aria-describedby; "Step 2 of 4: Team" and errors are announced in a polite live region
Continue looks dimmed while the step isn't valid but still answers, so keyboard and screen reader users hear what's missing
doc.Motion:
A finished step swaps its number for a check that draws itself in
Steps slide in from the side you're heading to with a short fade, while the old one slides out the other way
The card glides to the height of each step; the primary button glides to the width of its new label
An invalid field shakes once and its message folds in; chips pop in and fold away
The plan ring glides between cards; the success check pops in
With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly
doc.Responsive behavior:
Fills its container up to 520px and works down to 320px
Below 420px the steps collapse to "Step 2 of 4 · Team", plan cards stack and review rows wrap
Touch screens get 16px fields (no zoom on iOS) and buttons of at least 40px; the footer sticks to the bottom in long pages
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: A multi-step flow for onboarding and setup – steps that fill and check off, sliding steps, a card that morphs to each step, inline validation and a success state.

hoverStyle.transition: background-color 0.14s, opacity 0.2s, transform 0.14s, width 0.32s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), visibility 0.2s

doc.When to use:
A comments sidebar next to a document, design or record
Collaboration with an assistant that can apply edits people suggest with /edit
doc.When not to use: Long discussions with nested replies – use the Comment Thread for one conversation
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Tab	Move through tabs, sort, comments and the composer
Enter	Send the comment in the composer
doc.Accessibility:
Filters are tabs, sorting is a menu of radio items, resolve is a toggle button
Times are real time elements; the list announces new comments politely
doc.Motion: New comments fade in, edits show a spinner, the sort menu drops in – reduced motion turns this off
doc.Responsive behavior: Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Comment feed with filters, runnable /edit commands, resolve and a composer.

doc.When to use:
A single conversation attached to a selection, a cell or a line of text
Showing what an assistant did after someone asked for a change
doc.When not to use: A feed of many comments – use the Comments Panel
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Enter	Send the reply
Tab	Reach the status lines to fold their details open
doc.Accessibility:
Status lines are buttons with aria-expanded; folded details are inert
The thread announces new replies politely
doc.Motion: Replies fade in, the thinking text shimmers, details fold open – reduced motion turns this off
doc.Responsive behavior: Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: One comment with replies – an assistant reports what it did, folds open details and answers @mentions.

doc.When to use:
Suggesting the next step an app or assistant thinks is best – with a way out
Settings people rarely change but should get a nudge on, like sync modes or plans
doc.When not to use: Choices without a clear favorite – show them side by side instead
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Enter or Space	Fold the card, open alternatives or accept
Escape	Close the alternatives
doc.Accessibility:
The heading is a button with aria-expanded; alternatives are a menu of radio items
The signal is written out in words next to the bars
doc.Motion: The reason swaps softly when an alternative is picked; reduced motion turns this off
doc.Responsive behavior: Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Suggestion card with a confidence signal, alternatives to switch to and accept with undo.

doc.When to use:
Human-in-the-loop flows where an agent drafts an email and someone approves it – renewals, reminders, follow-ups
Inboxes or task lists of pending outreach, one card per record
doc.When not to use:
Writing long emails from scratch – use a full editor
Messages that go out without review – then a simple activity row is enough
doc.Keyboard interactions:
⌘ or Enter	Sends the email while editing
Esc	Leaves editing, or closes the recipient menu
doc.Accessibility:
The recipient is a button that opens a listbox; tones are toggle buttons with aria-pressed
The text is a plain paragraph; clicking it or the pencil swaps in a labelled text field
Sent and discarded states are announced as a status with an Undo button
doc.Motion:
Switching tone fades the new text in; the recipient menu scales in from its corner
Sending shows a spinner, then the card folds into a one-line receipt – the height glides between them
With prefers-reduced-motion changes happen instantly
doc.Responsive behavior:
Fills its container up to 520px; on narrow screens the email address and the shortcut hint hide
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Agent-written email for review – switch recipient and tone, edit inline, remove the attachment, send or discard with undo.

doc.When to use:
The usage or billing page of a SaaS or AI product – credits, tokens, minutes or messages per billing cycle
Showing what the usage went into (chat, search, images, API) next to plan limits like seats and storage
Nudging people to top up or upgrade right where they see they're running out
doc.When not to use:
Long-term trends over many months – a line chart like the KPI Chart reads better
More than about five categories – the bar gets too thin; group the small ones into "Other"
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Tab	Reaches the period switch, the bar, the sparkline and the button
← or →	Switch: picks the previous or next period. Bar: steps through the categories. Sparkline: steps through the days
Esc	Hides the category or day readout
doc.Accessibility:
A section labelled by its title; the bar and every limit are meters with their value as text ("7,420 of 10,000 credits")
The period switch is a radio group with a roving tab stop
The category tooltip is a polite live region, so stepping through the bar reads each part
Running low and reaching the limit are announced in a polite live region; amber is never the only signal – the text says it too
doc.Motion:
On first view the bar fills from zero and every number counts up, in one frame loop so numbers and widths stay in step
Switching periods: the white pill glides to the new option, numbers roll to their new values and the parts glide to their new widths
A category that drops out shrinks to nothing on the bar while its legend row folds away; the card glides to its new height
Hovering a part dims the others and highlights its legend row; the tooltip glides along the bar
Near the limit a small amber dot pops in and the button turns solid with a gentle nudge, its width gliding to the new label
With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly
doc.Responsive behavior:
Fills its container up to 460px; at 400px and below the switch gets its own row and the limits stack as rows
Works down to 320px wide; long labels end with an ellipsis, numbers and units never split
Touch: tapping a part or a legend row shows its value, targets grow to 36–38px
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Plan usage and AI credits – a stacked credits meter by category, daily sparkline, limits and a button that speaks up near the limit.

doc.When to use:
Dashboards that show one headline number and how its parts moved over a short period
Comparing a handful of channels, pages or plans day by day
doc.When not to use:
More than about six lines – the chart and the tooltip get hard to read
Long time ranges with hundreds of points – use a chart library with zoom and sampling
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Tab	Focus the chart
← or →	Move to the previous or next point
Esc	Close the tooltip
doc.Accessibility:
The chart is focusable and readable with the arrow keys
The tooltip is a polite live region, so screen readers announce the values of the current point
doc.Motion:
Lines draw in from the left on mount
Guide, dots and tooltip glide between points; reduced motion turns this off
doc.Responsive behavior:
The card fills its container up to 460px; the plot scales, line widths stay crisp
Touch works too – tap or drag across the chart
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Metric card with a multi-line chart and a tooltip that follows the pointer.

doc.When to use:
Small databases people edit in place – tools, vendors, budgets, contacts
Data that moves to and from Excel or Google Sheets with copy and paste
Lists where people pick several rows to act on
doc.When not to use:
Thousands of rows – add virtualisation, filters and server paging with a grid library
Editing one record with many fields – a form is clearer
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Arrow keys	Move the active cell
Shift or Arrow keys	Grow the selected range
⌘ / Ctrl or Arrow keys	Jump to the first or last row or column
Tab	Move to the next cell, Shift + Tab to the previous one
Enter or F2	Edit the active cell; Enter saves and moves down
Any character	Start editing with that character
Escape	Cancel an edit or collapse the range
Delete or Backspace	Clear the selected cells
⌘ / Ctrl or C / X / V	Copy, cut and paste – works with Excel and Google Sheets
⌘ / Ctrl or Z	Undo, add Shift to redo
⌘ / Ctrl or A	Select every cell
doc.Accessibility:
The table is a grid with selected cells marked, so screen readers follow the active cell and the range
Column headers are sort buttons and report the sort direction
Row checkboxes have labels; the header checkbox shows a mixed state when only some rows are checked
doc.Motion: Tag picker drops in, sort arrows turn, checkboxes pop – reduced motion turns all of it off
doc.Responsive behavior:
The table scrolls sideways inside the card on narrow screens instead of squeezing the columns
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Spreadsheet-style table: select cells and ranges, edit in place, copy and paste, undo and sort.

doc.When to use:
A ⌘K menu that runs actions across the tools your product connects to
Power users who want to reach any page or action without the mouse
doc.When not to use:
The only way to reach something – keep the main navigation visible as well
Fewer than five actions – buttons are easier to discover
doc.Keyboard interactions:
↑ or ↓	Move row by row through all sections
↵	Run the highlighted command
Tab	Jump to the next section (Shift Tab goes back)
⌘ or 1–5	Run a suggestion straight away (Ctrl on Windows)
Esc	Clear the field, then close
⌘ or K	Focus the field from anywhere
doc.Accessibility:
The field is a combobox that controls the list; the highlighted command is the active option
Groups are labelled, shortcut keys are hidden from screen readers
What just ran is announced in a polite live region
doc.Motion:
The gray highlight glides from row to row
The row that runs gives a short press; a check and its name appear in the tray below
With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly
doc.Responsive behavior:
Fills its container up to 600px; on phones shortcut keys and hints are left out
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Search and run anything from one field – tool actions with logos and ⌘1–⌘5, everyday commands with icons.

doc.When to use:
Switching between two to six views of the same content – sections of a dashboard, list / board / calendar, monthly / yearly
A choice that applies right away and where every option should stay visible
doc.When not to use:
More than six options or long labels – use a select or a menu
Choices that are confirmed with a Save button inside a form – radio buttons read clearer there
Turning one thing on or off – that's a switch
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Tab	Focuses the active option (one tab stop for the whole control)
← or →	Moves to and selects the previous or next option, wrapping around; ↑ ↓ too as a radiogroup
Home or End	Selects the first or last option
↵	Selects the focused option (Space works too)
doc.Accessibility:
A radiogroup with radios (aria-checked), or a tablist with tabs (aria-selected, aria-controls) with kind="tabs"
Roving tabindex: only the active option is in the tab order; disabled options are skipped by the arrow keys
The semibold copy of each label is aria-hidden, so names are read once; counts and badges are part of the name
Visible focus ring on the focused option
doc.Motion:
The indicator glides to the picked option; the edge facing the target leads, so it stretches a little and settles – calm, no bounce
Labels crossfade from regular to semibold while the semibold copy holds the width, so neighbours never shift
When a label or count changes, the option and the whole control morph to the new width and the pill follows; a new count blurs in
Pressing gives the pill a little (scale 0.97); dragging it across the options selects as you go
With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly
doc.Responsive behavior:
If it doesn't fit, it scrolls sideways with soft edges on the sides that hide options and keeps the active one in view
Touch screens: options are at least 40px tall; a tap picks on lift, so swiping to scroll never picks by accident
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Switch between two to six options – a raised pill or underline that glides, stretches a little and can be dragged across, with icons, counts and badges.

doc.When to use:
The integrations step of a command menu or settings dialog
Letting people find a service quickly and switch it on without leaving what they're doing
doc.When not to use:
A full marketplace with categories and many details per app – use a page instead
Two or three integrations – a simple list with switches is enough
doc.Keyboard interactions:
↑ or ↓	Move through the list
↵	Switch the picked integration on or off
Esc	Clear the search, then close
←	Back to the parent page when the search is empty
⌘ or /	Jump into the search from anywhere (Ctrl / on Windows)
doc.Accessibility:
The search is a combobox that controls the list; the picked row is announced as the active option
The connection switch is a real switch with a label that says what it will do
Details update in a polite live region when the pick changes
doc.Motion:
The gray highlight glides from row to row, also across the Connected and Available groups
The service tile swaps in with a short blur and lift; the arrows between the tiles turn once when connected
While connected, a ring keeps spreading out from the tiles – paused when the picker is off screen
With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly
doc.Responsive behavior:
Follows its own width: below 560px the list sits above the details; the illustration and capabilities are left out
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Integrations page of a command menu – search, a list of services and the picked one with its connection on two tiles.

doc.When to use:
Any action a user triggers: submit a form, send a message, open a dialog
Async actions that take a moment – the loading state keeps the label readable while it works
doc.When not to use:
Navigation to another page – use a link so it can be opened in a new tab
Switching between views – a segmented control or tabs show the current state
doc.Keyboard interactions: Enter or Space	Activate the button
doc.Accessibility:
A native button element, so focus, keyboard and form submission work as expected
While loading it stays focusable and announces aria-busy instead of becoming disabled
Icon-only buttons need an aria-label – the icon itself is hidden from screen readers
doc.Motion:
Pressing scales the button to 97%
Loading swaps the left icon for a spinner and sweeps a band across the label
When label or icon change, the width glides to the new size and the new content fades in from a soft blur
With prefers-reduced-motion the sweep stops and changes are instant
doc.Responsive behavior: Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Primary, secondary, ghost and destructive buttons with icons, sizes and a shimmering loading state.

doc.When to use:
Reactions under posts, comments or updates in a feed
Any toggle with a public count, like saves or upvotes
doc.When not to use: Actions that need a confirmation – a toggle gives none
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Tab	Move between the actions
Enter or Space	Toggle the focused action
doc.Accessibility:
Every action is a toggle button with aria-pressed and a label that includes its count
The rolling digits are decorative – the label carries the number
doc.Motion:
The icon shrinks, springs and fills with its color; the count glides to its new width and changed digits roll in
Reduced motion turns this off
doc.Responsive behavior: Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Like, comment, repost and share in one pill – icons pop and fill, counts roll in digit by digit.

Elif Yilmaz

doc.When to use:
Assigning people, labels, tags or projects – anything picked from a list that's too long to scan
Filters where several values can apply at once, like owners or statuses
Tag fields that should also accept new values (creatable)
doc.When not to use:
Up to five fixed choices – checkboxes or a segmented control show them all at once
Free text with no list behind it – use a plain input
Running actions rather than picking values – use the command menu
doc.Keyboard interactions:
↑ or ↓	Open the list, then move between rows
↵	Pick or unpick the active row (or create)
⌫	In the empty field: highlight the last chip, press again to remove it
Esc	Close the list; when closed, clear the typed text
Tab	Close the list and move on
doc.Accessibility:
Follows the ARIA combobox pattern: the input has role combobox with aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant; the list is a listbox with grouped options
Picked rows carry aria-selected, the listbox is aria-multiselectable in multiple mode
Picks and removals are announced in a polite live region, together with the count
Focus stays in the input while clicking rows and chip × buttons; the field shows a soft focus ring
doc.Motion:
Chips grow in with a small pop and fold away after a short flash; the field glides to its new height when chips wrap
A gray highlight glides to the active row; the list glides to its new height while filtering
Check marks pop in with a gentle spring; the "+3" chip and the count roll up or down
With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly
doc.Responsive behavior:
The list is as wide as the field, so it always fits the screen
Chips wrap onto new lines and long names truncate – works down to 320px
Touch screens get 44px rows, bigger chip buttons and 16px input text (no iOS zoom)
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Pick one or many from a searchable, grouped list – chips with avatars, highlighted matches, create-on-the-fly and full keyboard support.

doc.When to use:
Analytics, reports and dashboards where people switch between periods and compare them
Filters for bookings, invoices or logs that need a start and an end date
doc.When not to use:
A single date, like a birthday – a plain date field is quicker
Ranges that span many years – type the dates instead
doc.Keyboard interactions:
← or → or ↑ or ↓	Move day by day and week by week
PageUp or PageDown	Previous / next month
Home or End	Start / end of the week
↵	Pick the start, then the end
Esc	Close without applying
doc.Accessibility:
The trigger opens a dialog; each month is a grid and every day button has its full date as name
Today is marked with aria-current, picked days with aria-selected; the month name is announced when it changes
Focus moves with the arrow keys and returns to the trigger when the panel closes
doc.Motion:
The panel opens with a short scale and fade; months slide in from the side you're moving to
After the first click the band follows the pointer as a lighter preview until the second click
The comparison period appears as a gray band with outlined ends
With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly
doc.Responsive behavior:
Below 600px the presets turn into a scrolling row of chips and only the month the range ends in is shown; the footer stacks
The panel is as wide as the screen allows (up to 652px); set --ui-drp-panel-width, e.g. to 100%, to match your layout
Bigger day cells and buttons on touch screens
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Presets and two calendars with a hover preview, comparison with the previous period or year, full keyboard control.

doc.When to use:
Uploading documents, images or media – attachments, imports, asset libraries, onboarding
Several files at once, where people want to see what's done, what's still running and what failed
doc.When not to use:
A single avatar or logo – a simple picker with a preview is lighter
Huge uploads that run in the background for minutes – show them in a separate transfer panel
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Tab	Reaches the drop area, then Retry and Remove in every row
↵	On the drop area: opens the file picker (Space works too)
doc.Accessibility:
The drop area is a button that opens the file picker, described by the accepted types and size
Every row has a progress bar with its value; Retry and Remove are named after the file
Finished, failed and rejected files are announced in a polite live region
doc.Motion:
Dragging files over the area fans the three little documents out, the outline turns solid blue and the title counts the files
Rows grow in one after another; the bar fills in one solid color, a small check pops in when a file is done
A failed row gives a short shake and its bar turns red; removed rows fold away
With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly
doc.Responsive behavior:
Fills its container up to 520px; long file names are cut with an ellipsis
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Drag files in and watch them upload – fanning documents, colored type badges, progress with time left, errors with retry.

doc.When to use:
Short confirmations after an action – saved, copied, sent, moved to trash (with Undo)
Background work people started and want to hear back from – uploads, syncs, exports (toast.promise)
Errors that don't block the page, e.g. a sync that failed and can be retried later
doc.When not to use:
Errors in a form – show them next to the field
Anything people must read or decide on – use a dialog or an inline banner
Long-running progress with details – a progress panel or tracker fits better
doc.Keyboard interactions:
F8	Moves focus to the newest toast and fans the stack out
Tab	Goes from toast to toast, through their action and close buttons
Esc	Closes the focused toast (or the newest) and moves focus to the next one; focus returns where it was after the last
doc.Accessibility:
The stack is a labelled region ("Notifications (F8)"); every toast is focusable
New and updated toasts are read out in a polite status region – errors in an alert region, so they come first
The timer pauses while the pointer or keyboard focus is in the stack and while the tab is hidden, so nothing vanishes mid-read
Swiping is never the only way out: there's Esc and a named close button
Icons are decorative; color is limited to the success and error icons, the text says what happened
doc.Motion:
New toasts lift in from the edge; the ones behind move back, shrink a little and peek out
Hover or focus fans the stack out into a list – every toast is measured, so positions and heights glide
Promise toasts: the spinning arc closes into a ring while a check or cross draws in; the text crossfades and the card resizes
Closed toasts fade and sink a few pixels while the rest of the stack moves up; swiped toasts fly out in the swipe direction, short swipes rubber-band back
With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly – only the spinner keeps turning
doc.Responsive behavior:
356px wide on larger screens; under 600px it spans the width with 12px gutters (and respects the home indicator)
Touch: tap the stack to fan it out, swipe sideways or down to dismiss; close and action buttons get bigger hit areas
Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Calm toasts from anywhere – a stack that fans out on hover, promise toasts that morph from spinner to check, swipe to dismiss.

doc.When to use:
Onboarding with several areas, each made of a few steps that build on each other
A floating guide in a dashboard corner that people can fold away and come back to
doc.When not to use:
A single short list of steps – the Progress Tracker is lighter
Steps that can be done in any order – here each task unlocks the next
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Tab	Move between groups, tasks and header buttons
Enter or Space	Open or close a group, tick or untick a task
doc.Accessibility:
Group headers are buttons with aria-expanded, the closed panels are inert
Tasks that are not unlocked yet are disabled; finished ones are pressed toggle buttons
The bar is a progressbar with its percentage as value
doc.Motion:
Groups unfold smoothly; a finished group is struck through, folds away and opens the next one
Reduced motion turns the transitions off
doc.Responsive behavior: Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Onboarding panel with a progress bar and collapsible task groups that strike through when done.

doc.When to use:
Dashboards or agents that need a quick yes / no from a person before they continue
Approvals, renewals and alerts that can be answered with one click
doc.When not to use:
Decisions that need a form or a longer explanation – link to a page instead
Plain notifications without an answer – use a toast or an activity list
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Tab	Move between the answers and folded decisions
Enter or Space	Pick an answer or open a folded decision
doc.Accessibility:
The heading with the count is a live region, so the new count is announced
The confirmation after an answer is a status message; folded-away rows are inert
doc.Motion:
An answer turns into a green confirmation, then the row folds away and the next folded decision opens
Reduced motion skips the folding
doc.Responsive behavior: Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Open decisions with two quick answers each – answered ones confirm and fold away.

A few announcements or notices in a corner of an app – releases, maintenance, invites
Toast-style messages that stay until someone dismisses them
doc.When not to use:
Messages that need an answer before people continue – use a dialog
Many notifications at once – past three or four, use an inbox or activity list
doc.Keyboard interactions:
Tab	Move through the front card's buttons
Enter or Space	Run the action or dismiss the notice
doc.Accessibility:
The stack is a labelled region; each card is an article named by its title
Only the front card is read out and focusable; the next one takes its place after a dismiss
doc.Motion: A dismissed card slides away and the next one moves up into its place; reduced motion turns this off
doc.Responsive behavior: Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
doc._lead: Notice cards stacked behind each other – dismiss the front one to reveal the next.
